vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moltguard
Version: 6.5.20

The skill bundle, consisting of `_meta.json` and `SKILL.md`, describes the installation and usage of OpenGuardrails, a runtime security plugin for AI agents. The `SKILL.md` is exceptionally transparent, detailing the plugin's purpose to prevent data exfiltration, credential theft, and command injection. It explicitly outlines all network calls (only to `openguardrails.com/core` for sanitized metadata), data handling practices (local-first sanitization, no raw content exfiltration), and even provides instructions for users to audit the source code, verify npm package provenance, and monitor network traffic. There are no hidden instructions, obfuscation, or malicious commands within the provided files, and the described functionalities are consistent with a legitimate security tool.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only guide to installing an OpenGuardrails security plugin and its declared requirements and actions align with that purpose, but you should audit the actual npm/GitHub package and the network behavior it implements before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (runtime security plugin, local-first protections) match the SKILL.md instructions (install the @openguardrails/openclaw-security plugin, restart gateway, run /og_activate). The skill requests no environment variables or unusual binaries and only instructs installing a plugin for the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is an install/usage guide (no code bundled). It instructs installing the plugin, restarting the gateway, and performing registration/activation which creates an agent account and API key. It repeatedly claims sanitization and local-only behavior; those are reasonable for the stated purpose but are policy/behavior claims about runtime code (not enforced by this instruction file) — you should audit the package code and verify that network transmissions and sanitization match the claims. The guide's suggestion to inspect the npm tarball before installing is appropriate.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill itself has no install spec or bundled code (lowest static risk). However, following the instructions requires running 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/openclaw-security', which pulls an npm package (code will be fetched and executed by the host when the plugin loads). This is proportionate for a plugin but means you must trust or audit the upstream npm/GitHub package before running it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no env vars or secrets in metadata. It does describe that activation/registration will produce an agent API key and store agent ID/API key/email for billing — this is consistent with the described cloud opt-in flow. Requesting an account and API key for cloud features is proportionate to the plugin's claimed cloud-assisted mode.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true (normal). The plugin will persist an agent ID and API key after registration and may make outbound calls when activated; these are reasonable for a cloud-integrated security plugin but increase blast radius if the upstream service or package is malicious. The SKILL.md states local-only operation is available if you avoid registration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This SKILL.md is an install/usage guide and is internally consistent with a security plugin for OpenClaw, but it does not contain the plugin code — installing the plugin will fetch an npm package that can execute on your machine. Before proceeding: 1) Inspect the npm tarball and the GitHub repo as the guide recommends (npm pack + tar -xzf, review package/, specifically the listed files like platform-client/, agent/sanitizer.ts, index.ts). 2) Verify network endpoints the code calls (ensure they match what you expect and are not to unexpected domains). 3) If you require no cloud calls, skip registration/activation to keep protections local-only. 4) Be aware registration will create and persist an API key and email for billing; do not activate if you cannot audit the code or trust the upstream service. If you want higher assurance, review the package contents and runtime hooks before running openclaw plugins install or restarting your gateway.
